newsitem.title: USA: AT&T TO TEST NEW TOOL FOR LOCAL CALLS - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: AT&T TO TEST NEW TOOL FOR LOCAL CALLS - WSJ.

text.p: AT&T Corp will begin testing an electronic box that would advance the company's ambitions to offer local phone services nationwide, the Wall Street Journal said Monday in its electronic edition.

The report said the box would directly link home telephones to the AT&T wireless network. People familiar with the plan, which could be announced this week, told the paper that AT&T may charge as little as a 10 flat monthly fee to let users make unlimited local calls from their homes.
"This is the fixed wireless service that the industry has talked about for a long time as a means of replacing the twisted copper Bell line to the home," one executive said in the report.
The box, called a Personal Base Station, would sell for less than 300. The report said AT&T would pay the Baby Bells an access fee for carrying calls to their local customers.

The plan uses new wireless technology recently patented by the company, and it would be aimed at local phone customers now served by the Baby Bells, GTE Corp and other local phone companies, the report said.
